about: The interaction graph of the game: every screen, modal, panel and toast as a node, every user action that moves between them as an edge. It is the source of truth for the UI and tests/ui_graph_test.gd walks it. See docs/INTERACTION-GRAPH.md.

fixtures.$first: the first level of the campaign (open from the start)
fixtures.$locked: a level that is locked in a fresh save
fixtures.$inhibition: the m_inhibition level (its first-visit pointer is the one the walk shows)

ignore.why: The two arrow buttons of a stepper are part of the stepper, which is listed by its own id.
Value sliders of the parameter rows: they edit a number, they do not navigate.
The number box beside each value slider.
Read-only neuromodulator gauges drawn as sliders.
The built-in widgets of Godot's FileDialog; the dialog itself is the node lab.filedlg.

campaign.chapter.aplysia.label: Campaign chapter tab: Bestiary: Sea slug

campaign.chapter.fly_compass.label: Campaign chapter tab: Bestiary: Fly compass

campaign.chapter.fly_mb.label: Campaign chapter tab: Bestiary: Fly mushroom body

campaign.chapter.rates.label: Campaign chapter tab: Theory: Rate models

campaign.chapter.memory.label: Campaign chapter tab: Theory: Attractor memory

campaign.chapter.a_worm.label: Campaign chapter tab: Atlas: Reading wiring

campaign.chapter.a_compass.label: Campaign chapter tab: Atlas: A ring from wiring

lab.label: Lab frame: top bar, add-neuron palette, circuit editor (present in every lab state)

lab.atlas.label: Locked-wiring level (the development-only Atlas probe, SP_ATLAS in a debug build): engraved given wiring, one cell-type card per group in the inspector (sign toggle, scale stepper, or an active / silenced switch for a cell type that can be switched off), no way to add or delete cells and connections

lab.dx.label: Lab on a diagnosis case (read-only patient circuit)

lab.insp.brief.label: Inspector: the brief, what to build, the pass rule and recipe

lab.insp.ilink.label: Inspector: a link from a sensor to a cell selected

lab.insp.olink.label: Inspector: a link from a cell to a motor selected

lab.insp.in.label: Inspector: a sensor / noise input selected

lab.insp.lesion.label: Lesion lab (after a pass): cut, silence, re-run, sweep

lab.insp.dx.label: Diagnosis case card: symptoms, candidates, submit (shows probes and wrong guesses used)

lab.insp.dxpick.label: Diagnosis: a group or axon picked (read-only facts)

lab.dx.wrong.label: Diagnosis: a wrong answer was submitted

lab.dx.revealed.label: Diagnosis: answer revealed after three wrong tries

lab.parts_modal.label: Parts bin (pick the next neuron's type)

lab.import.label: Import from a passed level (your solved circuits, pasted as a group)

lab.endcard.label: Test x5 result card (worlds passed, stars, what to try next; Next level after a pass)

lab.result.passed.label: Score card after a pass: Next level, Results, Lesion lab, Analysis (no card rises over the bench)

lab.result.missed.label: Score card after a run that did not pass: the verdict (no card rises over the bench)

lab.checked.label: Score card with the Check result (written on the card, no toast)

lab.histo.label: Results card: your circuit against generated variants

lab.hint.label: Hint ladder card (idea, place, partial recipe)

lab.toast.label: Toast (Skip, hints unlocked, first pass, an error)

lab.stamp.label: First-pass celebration: the glow along the path, a toast, the notebook card (never blocks the bench)

tut.s1.label: Tutorial step 1: the bench, a sensor on the left and a motor on the right (Next)

tut.s2.label: Tutorial step 2: add a cell (lit: + Excitatory)

tut.s3.label: Tutorial step 3: connect the sensor to the cell (drag, or X then A with the pad)

tut.s4.label: Tutorial step 4: connect the cell to the motor (drag, or X then A with the pad)

tut.s5.label: Tutorial step 5: press Run (nothing runs until the player does)

tut.s6.label: Tutorial step 6: the raster and the trace, no spikes yet (Next)

tut.s7.label: Tutorial step 7: make the signal stronger: weight up, Run, until the cell fires

tut.s8.label: Tutorial step 8: the goal: fire on the big step only; change the weight, Run, read the score

tut.s10.label: Tutorial step 10: the result is on the score card (Next)

tut.s11.label: Tutorial step 11: the E / I switch on a second cell

tut.s12.label: Tutorial step 12: hints and the brief (Finish)

tut.picker.label: Tutorial step 13: pick a mode (Guided / Standard / Researcher) over the campaign map

tut.tip.label: One-step pointer, the first time a level with a new control opens (here m_inhibition: E / I)

edges.guard: an open level is not passed yet
edges.note: Continue opens the next open, unpassed spine level on an empty bench.
Selecting a pin shows the level's brief, stars and Build button in the detail panel.
Difficulty mode: Guided / Standard / Researcher.
Build opens an empty bench with the level's sensor and motor cards. Disabled while the level is locked.

edges.guard: Guided mode, or the level passed
edges.note: The reference circuit, already wired. Earns no stars.
A diagnosis case opens the patient's circuit.
The About row: Credits and licences.
Run starts the run (it never starts by itself); the button then reads Pause.
Adds a neuron and selects it.

edges.guard: from the level that first needs inhibition (always in the sandbox)
sandbox only: a level is scored on its own sensors, so a free noise input there would cap the score

edges.note: Connect mode: click a source, then a target.

edges.guard: from the level that first uses another cell type (always in the sandbox)

edges.note: Instant headless score of the circuit on five worlds; the result is written on the score card (a short progress card shows while it runs). Needs a wired circuit.

edges.guard: Guided, or Standard after two missed runs; never in Researcher

edges.note: Brief puts the level's brief back in the inspector.
Clicking a neuron group selects it.
Clicking a sensor card selects it.
Clicking a motor card selects it.
Dragging from one neuron's rim to another makes an axon and selects it.
Clicking the dashed link from a sensor card to a cell selects that one link.
Clicking the dashed link from a cell to a motor card selects that one link.
Clicking empty canvas clears the selection.
Disconnect removes that one sensor link.
Disconnect removes that one motor link.
Add a neuron, Undo: the circuit is back byte for byte; Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes it and Ctrl+Z undoes it again.
Add a neuron, Ctrl+Z, then Redo: the neuron is back.
The wheel zooms about the pointer (0.15x to 3x), middle-drag pans, F fits.
A sensor or motor card is dragged anywhere with the mouse; it stays (kept in the circuit), survives a reload, and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z move it back and again.
A sensor link and a motor link are each selected by a click and removed with Delete, one at a time; Ctrl+Z brings each back.
Click a group, shift-click another: both are selected; a box dragged over the empty bench selects what it covers.
Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V pastes a copy of every group; Ctrl+D duplicates; Ctrl+Z takes each back.
More > Save to A, change the bench, More > Load A: the saved circuit is back (asks first, the replaced bench is kept).

edges.guard: Load and Save tools are open (chapter II, the sandbox)
edges.note: More > Copy circuit as JSON, change the bench, More > Paste circuit JSON: checked by Circuits.validate, then it replaces the bench.

edges.guard: Load and Save tools are open
edges.note: Lists your saved bench and slots of every passed level; a pick is pasted as one selected group.
Skip to the next scripted event (or says there is none).
Picks the cell type the next added neuron is made from.
The player pressed Run and the episode ran to its end with a pass: the score card shows it and offers the ways on.
A circuit that does not pass runs to its end: the verdict is on the score card.

edges.guard: the level passed and a next level exists

edges.note: After the fifth seed the card turns into the end card with the 5-seed verdict.

edges.guard: the level passed and a next level exists

edges.note: Passing a level for the first time (the event calls the same celebration).
In the lesion lab a click on a group, axon or sensor toggles its lesion.
A sweep re-runs every single lesion; Cancel stops it.
Re-runs the episode on several seeds with the lesion (Cancel shows while it runs; the table appears when it is done, which the walk does not wait for).
Clicking a group shows read-only facts.
Play on a fresh save starts the tutorial in the lab (m_threshold, Guided, empty bench).
Play after the tutorial was skipped and no mode was ever chosen: the map with the one-screen mode picker.
Title > Play > Tutorial replays the tutorial at any time.
Do it for me adds the cell.
The player adds the cell with the lit palette button (a real click through the hole in the dim).
Do it for me wires the sensor to the cell.
A real mouse drag from the sensor card's edge onto the cell.
Do it for me wires the cell to the motor.
A real mouse drag from the cell's rim onto the motor card.
Do it for me presses Run.
The player presses the lit Run button: the run starts only now.
Do it for me sets a weight inside the band and presses Run; the step ends when the cell spikes.
A real click on the sensor card, the weight slider moved into the band, then a real click on Run.
The run the player started finishes and passes: the step ends by itself.
Do it for me sets the weight and presses Run; the step ends when the run passes.
Do it for me presses Check; the step ends when the result is on the score card.
The player presses the lit Check button.
Do it for me flips the second cell to inhibitory.
The player presses the lit E / I button.
Finish: the map opens with the mode picker.
Skip tutorial from the first run: marks it done and opens the map with the mode picker.
Skipping a replay goes straight to the map (the mode was chosen before).
Esc always leaves the tutorial.
Choosing a mode continues to the map.
Esc keeps the current mode and continues.
First visit to m_inhibition: the pointer at E / I.
Got it dismisses the pointer for good.

negatives.why: The reference circuit is hidden until the level is passed (Standard) and always offered in Guided.
A locked level cannot be built.
Hints open after two missed runs in Standard.
Test x5 sits on the bar only once the level is passed (always in Researcher).
The lesion lab opens after a pass.
